newsitem.title: GERMANY: Capital gains tax would hurt Germany, banker says.
newsitem.headline: Capital gains tax would hurt Germany, banker says.

text.p: Bayerische Vereinsbank AG chief executive Albrecht Schmidt said on Wednesday that a recent proposal to toughen the law on capital gains tax would damage Germany's standing as a financial centre.
"I view this proposal as more than damaging," Schmidt told a news conference in Munich. "It totally contradicts the debate about how to improve Germany's standing."

Current German law exempts investments from capital gains tax as long as gains are not realised for at least six months, but Chancellor Helmut Kohl's Christian Democrats recently mooted removing that exemption as part of broad tax reform.
Schmidt said the German real estate market had benefited from the current tax regime.
"Look at the German property market which has the advantage of being far more stable than in the United Kingdom, the United States or France," Schmidt said.
